---
title: "Lesson 3: Writing a Quarto page"
---

Every page of a Quarto website is a `.qmd` file with three kinds of content:

1. A **YAML header** with the page's settings
2. **Markdown** text
3. Optional **code chunks** that Quarto runs

## A complete example page

````markdown
---
title: "Weekly ILI Summary"
author: "Jane Smith"
date: 2026-10-28
---

## Overview

This page shows **made-up** influenza-like illness (ILI) data
for practice.

::: {.callout-note}
All data on this page is synthetic.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-ili
#| echo: true
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of weekly percent ILI over 20 weeks, rising from
#|   about 1.5% to a peak near 4.5% in week 12, then falling."

library(ggplot2)

set.seed(2026)
ili <- data.frame(
  week    = seq(as.Date("2025-09-28"), by = "week", length.out = 20),
  pct_ili = round(1.5 + 3 * exp(-((1:20 - 12)^2) / 18) + rnorm(20, 0, 0.2), 1)
)

ggplot(ili, aes(week, pct_ili)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "% ILI")
```

The peak was in week `{r} which.max(ili$pct_ili)`.
````

Rendered, this produces a page with a title, author and date, a heading, a blue note box, the R code, the chart, and a sentence with the peak week filled in from the data.

## 1. The YAML header

The block between the two `---` lines at the very top. It's written in **YAML**: `key: value` pairs.

```yaml
---
title: "Weekly ILI Summary"
author: "Jane Smith"
date: 2026-10-28
description: "One-line summary, used by search and link previews"
---
```

::: {.callout-warning title="YAML is picky about spacing"}
- There must be a space after the colon: `title: "Hi"`, not `title:"Hi"`.
- Indent with **spaces**, never tabs.
- Put text in quotes if it contains a colon: `title: "Lesson 1: Basics"`.
:::

## 2. Markdown

Quarto uses the same Markdown as GitHub READMEs, plus a few extras.

| You type | You get |
|---|---|
| `## Heading` | Section heading (use `##` and below; the title is the top level) |
| `**bold**` / `*italic*` | **bold** / *italic* |
| `- item` / `1. item` | Bulleted / numbered list |
| `[text](https://example.com)` | A link |
| `[next lesson](04-create-website.qmd)` | A link to another page. Use the `.qmd` name; Quarto converts it to `.html` |
| `` `code` `` | Inline `code` |
| `> quote` | A block quote |

### Callouts

Colored boxes for notes, tips, and warnings:

```markdown
::: {.callout-tip}
Save often!
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Careful"}
This deletes files.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Hidden until clicked: great for exercise answers.
:::
```

Types: `callout-note`, `callout-tip`, `callout-warning`, `callout-important`, `callout-caution`.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Like this one.
:::

### Tabs

Tabs let readers choose between versions, like the editor tabs in this training:

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}
## Mac
Press Cmd + S.
## Windows
Press Ctrl + S.
:::
```

## 3. Images and alt text

```markdown
![](images/epi-curve.png){fig-alt="Bar chart of weekly measles cases, peaking at 12 in week 8."}
```

- **`fig-alt`** is the **alt text**: what screen-reader users hear instead of seeing the image. **Every image needs it.**
- Text inside the square brackets `![like this](...)` becomes a **visible caption** under the image. Leave the brackets empty if you don't want a caption.
- Good alt text says what the image shows and its main point, not just "chart" or "screenshot."

## 4. R code chunks

A chunk starts with ```` ```{r} ```` and ends with ```` ``` ````. Options go at the top, on lines starting with `#|`:

```{{r}}
#| label: summary-table
#| echo: false

head(ili)
```

Common options (each goes on its own `#|` line):

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `label: name` | Names the chunk (no spaces). Labels starting with `fig-` make numbered, cross-referenceable figures |
| `echo: false` | Hide the code, show only the result |
| `eval: false` | Show the code, but don't run it |
| `include: false` | Run the code, but show nothing (useful for loading packages) |
| `warning: false` | Hide warnings |
| `fig-alt: "..."` | Alt text for a chart (**required for every chart**) |
| `fig-cap: "..."` | Visible caption for a chart |

You can set options for every chunk on a page in the YAML header:

```yaml
---
title: "My page"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
---
```

### Inline code

Put R results into a sentence with `` `{r} expression` ``:

```markdown
There were `{r} nrow(cases)` cases this week.
```

::: {.callout-important title="Never use real data on a public site"}
Code on a website runs **when you render**, and its results are published. Use made-up (synthetic) or public data only. See [Data security](../intro-to-github/09-data-security.qmd).
:::

## 5. Visual mode

All three editors have a **visual editor** that shows a `.qmd` file formatted (like a word processor), with toolbar buttons for headings, lists, and tables.

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## Positron

Right-click in the file → **Edit in Visual Mode**, or press **Cmd + Shift + F4** (Mac) / **Ctrl + Shift + F4** (Windows). Same again to switch back.

## VS Code

Right-click in the file → **Edit in Visual Mode**, or press **Cmd + Shift + F4** (Mac) / **Ctrl + Shift + F4** (Windows). Requires the Quarto extension.

## RStudio

Click **Visual** / **Source** at the top left of the editor.

:::

Visual mode may reformat your Markdown slightly when it saves (spacing, table layout). That's harmless.
